Question: Of the Gurkha soldiers stationed in Great Britain are most of them Hindus and if so are they vegetarians? What is the Royal army diet composed of for the vegan and non vegan Gurkhas and could their diet whatever it is, be used for strength training?
Answer: Dietary restrictions follow the caste and region not religion in India. For example, Brahmins in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh are banned from not only eating meat but also onion and garlic. But Brahmins in Bengal eat fish and seafood without problems (though they can’t eat onion or garlic). And Brahmin Christians (yes, in India there is such a thing) also tend to be vegetarians. People who are from marginal farming places (such as Nepal) tend to be meat eaters.

Question: What economic and cultural factors led to the end of the Cold War?
Answer: Mikhail Gorbachev grew up in the Soviet system. He was convinced that it was the right system. He could see that it had problems (there are no flawless systems) but believed that the flaws could be fixed. Then, at a relatively young age, he became the head of USSR. And the more he tried to learn, the more he realized that there was rot in the system. So, he decided that the system could be reformed and the rot could be taken out without destroying the system - through openness and restructuring. What he did not realize (or realized but had no other choice) was that change creates its own momentum. The moment people realized that the system’s own guardians (the powerful elite) are not vested in it, they decided that they want even more freedom than what was on the table. And everything unraveled from there on. USSR’s dire economic situation can be chalked up to their low productivity, caused by lack of even basic controls. Many in the US claim that accelerated military spending by Reagan triggered USSR’s downfall. This is a convenient narrative drummed up by people who want to grant sainthood to Reagan.

Question: How much sleep do you get?
Answer: Reading the other answers I feel damned lucky. I get ~7.5 hours of sleep every night. Sure, it ranges a bit (somewhere between 6.5 and 9 hours). I have, due to many reasons, transformed myself into an early bird. My goal is to be in bed by 9pm (usually I am in bed about 9:15) and wake up at 5am (when the alarm goes off). On weekends, the alarm is set to 7:30am. I have noticed that I need a minimum of 6 hours of sleep, unless I am running on adrenalin. And if my sleep is uninterrupted, I rarely need more than 7 hours. But, as I get older, my sleep is becoming more brittle - I wake up to loud noises and it takes me a good 10–20 minutes to truly fall back asleep. When I was in my 20s, it used to take me 5 seconds to fall back asleep. When I am traveling (plane, bus, train or taxi), I focus on sleeping by (please don’t laugh) consciously switching off parts of my body (legs, arms, back, neck, stomach etc). Luckily because I am not tall, I can curl up in smaller spaces. As a result, I minimize travel-related exhaustion.
